what_was_done: (1) RUN_TIER_ADOPTION_RE matches only a dotted member chain on an input object ending in '|| null' (a.tier, s.config.tier_override, survey.config.tier_override), and workflow_problems skips it only when the chain names no TIER, ROLE or OVERRIDE. RUN.tier = TIER.planner, RUN.tier = TIER.reviewer || null, RUN.tier = a.tier || TIER.planner, RUN.tier = a.tier and RUN.tier = 'planner' are each rejected now (test_pinning_the_run_to_a_tier_is_rejected; the old loose regex accepted the first three). (2) _strip_comments_and_strings scans a template literal's ${...} interpolations as code, so a direct agent(, a model:/effort: literal and a forbidden workflow('vsdd-factory:release') written inside a template are reported (test_interpolations_are_scanned_as_code). A regular-expression literal is opaque: escapes and [...] classes hold no terminator, flags are consumed, and a regex that does not close before the line's newline reads as division, so a quote inside /'/g no longer throws the string state off and a following direct agent( is reported (test_a_regex_literal_hides_nothing_after_it). (3) The stripping is pinned by tests that fail with it removed: test_a_comment_and_a_prompt_string_are_not_tier_settings (a comment 'the agent (x)' and a prompt string 'effort: high' trip nothing) was checked by mutation to fail with js = body. (4) The data-key question is decided and tested: a model:/effort: key whose value is carried ({ model: u.model, effort: u.effort }) passes what the run was given and is allowed; one set from a quoted literal is a tier setting and is rejected (TIER_KEY_RE narrowed; test_a_carried_model_data_key_is_not_a_tier_setting, both halves). Lint suite: 85 passed, 1 skipped.
